$ETH  Now 1918, climbing back to the bottom of that wall in 1925 and grinding. The script really hasn’t changed at all. Grinding for a whole week—rubbing back and forth from 1885 to 1925, pull a bit, ease a bit; even the edge by the wall can’t be broken through.

Outside, the crowd pulling the wagon is still shouting as fiercely as ever. ETF saw another inflow of over seventy million. Institutions are buying, and the big holders adding on top are increasing their positions too. Sentiment score has even dried up to more than seven. The bullish threads get over four hundred posts in a day—everything that can be hyped has been hyped to the max.

But if you split the money open and look at it, it’s not funny. In spot trading, in three hours there are twelve candles and not a single one is green; net outflow of over a hundred thousand. Big orders are still being pulled out. Aggressive sell orders are pressing down to hit buy orders. That little bit of replenishment every 15 minutes—what’s that supposed to do?

The contracts side is lively though. The share of aggressive buys has reached 58%. Whale accounts are still piling into long orders, and retail traders are even more—over seventy percent holding longs. The fees are pitifully low; nobody is paying interest. It’s all people holding their ground empty-handed.

In plain terms: pushing upward relies on sentiment and the futures/contract side, while the spot market underneath keeps leaking water. Whether the wall can be pierced depends on whether this water can be replenished. I won’t chase. I’ll wait—wait until the wall breaks, then when it retraces and someone picks it up, I’ll decide. If you charge in from this position, you’re just delivering ammunition to the wagon outside.

If ETH can hold above 1,900 and break 1,930 with volume, I might consider adding a bit of position; my stop-loss would be at 1,860, and my initial target would be 1,980. This is just my trading idea—do your own weighing.

Next, let’s talk about today’s biggest gainers. Honestly, at first I thought the data for these three must be wrong. BTW, +57.78% straight away—at a price of 0.56 U, it traded 360 million U in volume over 24 hours. The hype is even hotter than BTC. ACE is also going crazy: +55.33%, at 0.237 U, with 700 million U in volume. But this guy’s funding rate is -0.2736%, meaning shorts are overheated. VELVET is a bit more normal: +36.51%, and a funding rate of 0.0177%, which is still relatively healthy.

BTW, this coin—people say it’s the governance token of the Bitway ecosystem—was number one on the trending list, with huge trading activity. But the funding rate is 0.1020%, and longs are a bit overheated. Honestly, I wouldn’t chase something like this. If you’re itching to trade, just play with a small position, set your stop-loss properly, and don’t ask me how I know—I lost money on coins like this before. As for ACE: it’s a game concept coin, an “AAA blockbuster,” sounds big and impressive, but with that funding rate being so negative, it suggests the futures market has a lot of people looking bearish. And yet the price is up 55%—this round of shorts is probably feeling pretty uncomfortable. Still, I don’t recommend chasing; with volatility like this, your heart can’t take it.

VELVET is the only strong coin I’d say is “normal-ish” today: +36.51%, funding rate is normal, and volume is fine too. If it can pull back to around 0.60 and not break it, I think you could try a small long position. Stop-loss at 0.57, target 0.75. Of course, this is just my personal thinking. Altcoins have big risks—don’t go all-in and gamble everything.

Now look at the biggest losers: GPS -27.48%, JCT -25.90%, BEAT -22.89%. These were bouncing around on the trending lists a few days ago, and today they’re cold. Honestly, for coins that pump and dump like that, I usually just blacklist them right away. If you chased them earlier, you’re probably questioning life by now. But it’s okay—this is how the market works. Today you laugh at others, tomorrow others laugh at you. We’ve all been the person “standing guard at the top.”

Finally, let’s talk about SOL and PUMP. In the trending section there’s Solana and Pump.fun, which suggests on-chain hype is still there. SOL isn’t on the gainers list, but as the ecosystem leader, as long as the chain is active, it won’t be too bad. My own idea is: if SOL pulls back to around 140, you could buy a little in batches, with a target of 155. Pump.fun is a meme coin launcher—hype is still there, but I won’t touch it. It’s too stimulating; I’m afraid my heart can’t handle it.

To sum it up: right now the market is “BTC is steady, alts are flying—but what’s flying is basically a lottery ticket.” BTC and ETH are suitable for holding patiently and waiting for direction. As for altcoins, either don’t touch them, or if you do, use money you can afford to lose—don’t gamble with everything. Don’t ask me which one can 10x—I’d have retired early if I knew.

Lastly, do you think coins like BTW can still be chased? Or is this just a “one-day tour” kind of行情? Chat in the comments—I want to see your courage.

Glamsterdam goes live for official testing tomorrow: Ethereum this time is deliberately letting everyone “break” the system first
Ethereum has already launched the Platåberget public testnet, but the real Glamsterdam fork will be activated on August 20. This network will run for several months, with a very direct purpose: first let developers, node operators, wallets, and staking services surface the issues by running into them, then move on to Sepolia and Hoodi, and only afterward come to the mainnet.
In other words:
This isn’t an upgrade to the ETH mainnet tomorrow—it’s the opening of a public “crash test arena.”
This round of changes isn’t small: ePBS is being restructured for block production, BAL is laying the groundwork for future parallel execution, the contract size limit increases from 24KiB to 64KiB, and there will also be large-scale Gas re-pricing. The official team even warns that any wallets, indexers, or Gas estimators that have hardcoded the maximum Gas Limit need to be updated.
The bigger goal is to further scale Ethereum L1. The official roadmap has positioned Glamsterdam as the Q4 2026 upgrade, with the core focus on parallelization, higher capacity, and controlling state bloat.
So what really matters tomorrow isn’t whether ETH pumps or not, but:
Can these new underlying rules be “tortured” in a public environment without breaking?
#ETH  #Ethereum #以太坊启动glamsterdam早期测试网

A major upgrade doesn't automatically mean ETH goes up.
We've seen this before across crypto.
Strong headlines can create short-term excitement, but eventually the market asks a much harder question:
Is there real demand behind the story?
For Ethereum, Glamsterdam matters because upgrades are ultimately about improving the network's infrastructure and ability to support more activity.
But investors will be watching what happens beyond the announcement.
👀 More users?
👀 More transactions?
👀 More applications?
👀 More capital entering Ethereum?
That's where the real story starts.
ETH doesn't need another headline.
It needs sustained demand to absorb the available supply.
And that's why I'm more interested in what happens after the Glamsterdam excitement fades.
If adoption and network activity start accelerating, the upgrade could become much more meaningful for ETH.
If activity doesn't follow, the market may eventually move on to the next narrative.
The testnet is the beginning of the story — not the conclusion.

In essence, it’s the Fed injecting USD liquidity into the market. The last time USD liquidity expanded dramatically—was also the underlying fuel for the BTC rally that pushed it from $30,000 all the way to $60,000.

The market is in a typical liquidity vacuum period, waiting for a macro catalyst. This thesis is worth watching because it ties what seems unrelated to crypto—yen depreciation—directly to the main driver: USD supply.

Short term: Pure narrative; price may not react immediately. Macro traders need to see evidence of actual Bank of Japan intervention, or a U.S.–Japan currency swap getting executed, before they step in. Within the next 12 hours, BTC will most likely continue to range around the $64.0k area.

Medium term: Once this logic is validated—e.g., Japan’s Ministry of Finance intervenes in FX markets at a large scale, with the Fed providing dollars—that would be a textbook-level liquidity positive, similar to the post–March 2020走势 (price action). Neynar admits it did not meet targets and initiates Farcaster operations handover

The decentralized social protocol Farcaster is once again at a crossroads for operational ownership transfer. On August 18, Neynar co-founder Rishav Mukherji publicly stated that the company has begun the process of finding new homes and an operations team for Farcaster, Clanker, and Neynar-related products. The company is currently in discussions with several teams that may be suitable to operate decentralized social applications and developer-oriented products. He also acknowledged that Neynar failed to achieve the goals it set when it took over earlier this year, and that the current team is not a good fit for the next phase of development.

To understand the context, it helps to go back to two earlier handovers. Farcaster was founded by former Coinbase executive Dan Romero and Varun Srinivasan. Initially, their company Merkle Manufactory developed it with the goal of separating social accounts and relationship graphs from a single platform, so that developers could build different clients around a unified identity and social data. After about five years of development, Merkle raised approximately $180 million. On January 21, 2026, the two founders transferred the protocol contracts, codebase, Farcaster application, and Clanker to Neynar and stepped away from day-to-day operations. Before the handover, Neynar was already an important ecosystem infrastructure provider, offering nodes, interfaces, databases, and data pipelines to developers.

The core facts in this case are relatively clear: Neynar says the applications and developer products will continue to run as usual for now, with no direct impact on users. The company will return treasury funds on the books, with most of the funds still being retained; team members then move on to new projects. However, the identities of the receiving party, the deal structure, the handover timing, and whether the protocol, clients, Clanker, and Neynar’s developer business are being transferred as a whole—or whether they are instead seeking different operators—remain undecided. Other reports indicate that Farcaster protocol revenue fell from about $35.43 million in Q1 2026 to about $3.77 million between July 1 and August 17, suggesting commercial traction and growth are under pressure.

From a logical standpoint, Neynar is not making zero progress. After taking over, it reduced infrastructure operating costs by about 80%, increased operations by validators distributed across different regions, and opened protocol code previously accessible only to the core team to these operating parties. It also plans to move the decision on new validators to on-chain voting by the existing validator chain. These actions increase the protocol’s ability to operate independently of a single company. But Mukherji characterized current conditions as follows: a tightly knit community, a flagship application with operating costs that are not low, and a market where growth is slow. This mix needs to align with Neynar’s different organizational and funding structure. Farcaster uses a hybrid architecture: account identity and key management are located in OP Mainnet contracts, while high-frequency data such as posts, follows, and interactions are stored by the Snapchain validator network. Protocol data can be read by multiple parties, but ongoing investment is still required for product development in official clients, content distribution, customer support, wallet functionality, and developer interfaces. Therefore, Neynar stepping away from day-to-day operations does not mean the protocol stops running; rather, the consumer-side products still heavily depend on an operating entity willing to carry long-term costs.

The impact path on the crypto market is more reflected in the narrative around the sector and ecosystem expectations, rather than in immediate volatility of a single asset. Web3 social platforms have repeatedly faced the division-of-labor challenge: “protocols can be open, but flagship applications are hard to sustain.” Before the first ownership change of Farcaster, Lens also transferred day-to-day product operations to Mask Network. If consumer-side growth cannot sustainably cover operating investments over the long term, the new operator may be more inclined to split assets, reduce product lines, or focus on developer tools and specific vertical scenarios. For existing users and third-party developers, the short-term usage and data reading paths remain; in the long term, it will depend on whether the new operator continues the client experience, wallet, and transaction capabilities, and whether surrounding products such as Clanker are also jointly carried over. If the treasury repayment arrangement is implemented gradually, it will also influence outside judgments about the balance sheets of the relevant entities and their willingness to invest further.

Editorial observation suggests that, at this stage, the message should be defined as “re-matching the operating party,” not as the protocol itself becoming invalid. Items still to confirm include potential receiving parties, whether products will be split, who the on-book fund repayment will go to and on what timeline, and whether validator governance is progressing as scheduled. Until these pieces of information are clarified, Farcaster remains under Neynar’s operation of the existing product, and the third operational structure has not yet formed. Market discussions should distinguish between disclosed facts and handover details that have not been made public, to avoid equating “seeking a new operator” directly with an ecosystem shutdown.

content:
Neynar承认未达目标 启动Farcaster运营交接

去中心化社交协议Farcaster再一次走到运营权交接的关口。Neynar联合创始人Rishav Mukherji于8月18日公开表示，公司已启动为Farcaster、Clanker以及Neynar相关产品寻找新归宿和运营团队的流程，目前正与数个可能适合运营去中心化社交应用及开发者产品的团队接触。他同时承认，Neynar未能实现年初接手时设定的目标，现有团队也不适合下一阶段发展。

事件背景需要回到更早的两次交接。Farcaster由前Coinbase高管Dan Romero与Varun Srinivasan创办，最初由两人的公司Merkle Manufactory开发，目标是把社交账户与关系网络从单一平台中拆出，让开发者围绕同一套身份与社交数据构建不同客户端。经过约五年开发，Merkle累计融资约1.8亿美元。2026年1月21日，两位创始人将协议合约、代码库、Farcaster应用及Clanker交给Neynar，并退出日常运营。Neynar在交接前已是生态重要基础设施服务商，为开发者提供节点、接口、数据库与数据管道。

本次核心事实相对清晰：Neynar称应用与开发者产品暂时照常运行，对用户没有直接影响；公司将返还账面资金，其中大部分资金仍然保留，团队成员随后转向新项目。但接手方身份、交易结构、交接时间，以及协议、客户端、Clanker与Neynar开发者业务是整体转让还是分别寻找运营方，目前均未确定。另有报道指出，Farcaster协议收入从2026年第一季度的约3543万美元，降至7月1日至8月17日期间约37.7万美元，侧面说明商业化与增长承压。

从逻辑上看，Neynar并非毫无进展。接手后其将基础设施运行成本降低约80%，增加分布在不同地区的验证者运营方，并向这些运营方开放此前仅核心团队可访问的协议代码库，还计划把新增验证者决定交给现有验证者链上投票。这些动作提高了协议脱离单一公司的能力。但Mukherji把当前条件概括为：紧密的社区、运营成本不低的旗舰应用，以及增长缓慢的市场。这套组合需要与Neynar不同的组织与资金结构。Farcaster采用混合架构，账户身份与密钥管理位于OP Mainnet合约，帖子、关注与互动等高频数据由Snapchain验证者网络保存；协议数据可被多方读取，而官方客户端的产品开发、内容分发、客服、钱包功能及开发者接口仍需持续投入。因此，Neynar退出日常运营并不等于协议停止运行，但消费端产品仍高度依赖愿意长期承担成本的运营主体。

对加密市场的影响路径，更多体现在赛道叙事与生态预期，而非单一资产的即时波动。Web3社交近年反复出现“协议可开放、旗舰应用难持续”的分工难题：Farcaster第一次易主前一天，Lens也曾将日常产品运营交给Mask Network。若消费端增长长期无法覆盖运营投入，接手方可能更倾向拆分资产、收缩产品线，或把重点放在开发者工具与特定垂直场景。对现有用户与第三方开发者而言，短期使用与数据读取路径仍在；中长期则取决于新运营方是否延续客户端体验、钱包与交易能力，以及Clanker等周边产品是否被一并承接。资金返还安排若逐步落地，也会影响外界对相关主体资产负债表与后续投入意愿的判断。

编辑观察认为，现阶段更应把消息定性为“运营主体再匹配”，而不是协议本身失效。待确认事项仍包括潜在接手方、产品是否拆分、账面资金返还对象与节奏，以及验证者治理是否如期推进。在这些信息明确前，Farcaster仍由Neynar维持现有产品运行，第三次运营结构尚未成形。市场讨论宜区分已披露事实与尚未公开的交接细节，避免把寻找运营方直接等同于生态停摆。

To be honest, seeing the market today, my first reaction wasn’t excitement—it was a bit of警觉 (alert).

BTC is ranging sideways at 64,380, up just 1% over 7 days. This isn’t really a行情 (market setup); it’s more like the market is dozing off. The Fear & Greed Index is 50, right in the middle—neither bulls nor bears are getting their way. At this point, the most dangerous thing isn’t picking the wrong direction; it’s when you feel the direction is crystal clear.

But what really had my attention was BTW: in the last 24 hours it surged 84.53%, with trading volume of $548 million. Number one on the hot search, funding rate 0.0613%—bulls are getting overheated. Honestly, I’ve seen price-and-volume surge like this many times in a bull market, but every time the ending is a little different. The “Bitway” ecosystem narrative is indeed imaginative, but a doubling move in one day feels more like emotion driving the price rather than a value reassessment. If you’ve got coins in hand, consider this: when everyone is talking about one coin, it often means the incremental capital has already come in for the most part.

VELVET and HEMI are also doing well—up 35% and 22%—but the funding rates are still relatively normal, suggesting leveraged longs chasing price aren’t that out of control. That’s healthier than BTW.

What’s really interesting is ACE: it ranks 4th on the gainers list, up 20.6%, but its funding rate is -0.1668%—shorts are overheated. This is a classic contrarian indicator scenario: everyone is desperately bearish, yet the price keeps climbing. Personally, I like watching this kind of divergence because it often means the fuel for short covering hasn’t burned out yet. If ACE can hold today’s gains, there may be another window for momentum upside over the next few days.

Now let’s talk about the names that got hit hard. JCT is down 29.96% today, and the funding rate is 0.0050% (looks normal), but falling three-tenths in a day suggests the coin/position structure has problems. The top five on the losers list are all double-digit declines. This reminds us: the current market isn’t broad-based “everything is up” action—it’s an extremely polarized game of limited supply.

From another angle, this kind of market can actually be pretty good to trade. The overall index is moving sideways, while money rotates among localized sectors. Opportunities are concentrated in a handful of coins with real narratives. The key is: don’t chase; wait for pullbacks.

As for a more concrete trading approach: BTC is consolidating in the 64,000–64,500 range. If it dips back around 63,500, you could consider a slightly long-biased direction; set your stop-loss at 62,800 and target 65,800. ETH is relatively stronger: there’s support around 1,920. If it pulls back to around 1,880, you can look for long-biased opportunities; stop-loss at 1,840 and target 1,980.

For altcoins, I suggest focusing on ACE’s pullback opportunity. If it can retrace to the 50% level of its upswing, and it lines up with the short funding rate, you might get a wave of “repair” in the price action. I don’t recommend chasing BTW—sentiment is too hot. Stay calm and analyze: this kind of move usually needs a decent washout to digest profit-taking.

Finally, I’ll be blunt: there’s a ton of noise in the market right now. The hot search buzz around Pump.fun and Solana shows meme sentiment is still alive. But I think rather than chasing things that have already flown, it’s better to be patient and wait for opportunities that haven’t been priced in enough yet.

What do you think about ACE’s short overheating—trap or opportunity? Let’s chat in the comments.

content:
说实话，看到今天这个盘面，我第一反应不是兴奋，反而有点警觉。

BTC在64,380横着，7天涨了1%，这哪是行情，这分明是市场在打盹。恐惧贪婪指数50，刚好卡在中间，多空谁都不服谁。这时候最危险的不是方向选错，而是你觉得方向很明确。

但真正让我盯着看的是BTW，24小时拉了84.53%，成交额5.48亿美金。热搜第一，资金费率0.0613%，多头过热。说实话，这种量价齐升的场面在牛市里见过太多次，但每次结局都不太一样。Bitway这个生态叙事确实有想象力，但一天翻倍的走法，我觉得更像是情绪驱动而非价值重估。如果你手里有筹码，不妨想想：当所有人都在讨论一个币的时候，往往意味着增量资金已经进得差不多了。

VELVET和HEMI也都涨得不错，35%和22%，但资金费率还算正常，说明追高的杠杆资金没那么疯。这点比BTW健康。

真正有意思的是ACE，涨幅榜第四，涨了20.6%，但资金费率是-0.1668%，空头过热。这是一个典型的反向指标场景——大家拼命看空，价格却一路走高。Personally，这种背离我喜欢关注，因为它往往意味着空头回补的燃料还没烧完。如果ACE能守住今天的涨幅，接下来几天可能还有惯性上冲的机会。

再说说跌得狠的，JCT今天-29.96%，资金费率0.0050%看着正常，但一天跌三成说明筹码结构出了问题。跌幅榜前五全是两位数下跌，这提醒我们：现在的市场不是普涨行情，而是极度分化的存量博弈。

换个角度看，这种行情其实挺好做的。大盘横盘，资金在局部板块轮动，机会集中在少数几个有真实叙事的币种上。关键是别追高，等回调。

具体到交易思路，BTC在64,000-64,500这个区间震荡，如果回踩63,500附近可以考虑偏多方向，止损放在62,800，目标看65,800。ETH相对强一点，1,920附近有支撑，回踩1,880可以关注偏多机会，止损1,840，目标1,980。

山寨这边，我建议关注ACE的回踩机会。如果它能回调到涨幅的50%位置，配合空头资金费率，可能有一波修复行情。BTW我不建议追了，情绪太热，冷静分析一下，这种走法往往需要一次像样的洗盘来消化获利盘。

最后说句实话，现在市场的噪音特别多，热搜榜上Pump.fun和Solana的热度说明meme情绪还在。但我觉得，与其追那些已经飞起来的，不如耐心等那些还没被充分定价的机会。

Uniswap Labs has expanded its own Liquidity Layer to the Arc network. Arc is a new chain focused on compliance, and its target customers are institutions. Plainly put: previously, institutions wanted to play DeFi but found on-chain environments too wild and compliance too uncertain; a permissioned network like Arc is built for them, and Uniswap is laying its strongest liquidity supply directly across. The focus is stablecoin trading—this is the most real demand from institutions. Cross-border settlement, tokenized Treasuries, and in the end, it all comes down to buying, selling, and liquidity depth for stablecoins. One-sentence translation: Uniswap isn’t competing for retail users—it’s setting up shop at the institutions’ doorstep.

- Medium term: a substantive signal for the DeFi landscape. The combination of a compliant chain plus native liquidity suggests that leading protocols have already effectively assumed that the “institutional entry point” is the next major battleground for incremental growth. Whether Arc can take off remains uncertain, but Uniswap has moved early—there’s a fairly good chance it will capture some of the upside.

My take
Neutral to slightly bullish in terms of direction. This is a long-term narrative positive, not a short-term catalyst. If ETH holds around the $1,900 level, and when sentiment in the DeFi sector rebounds, assets like UNI should show greater upside elasticity. The risk: the “institutional” story has been called for three years, yet the incremental execution has consistently fallen short of expectations—Arc could also just be another compliance chain nobody uses. If BTC loses the $64,000 level, then no narrative will matter. My view: note this collaboration, and wait for on-chain stablecoin data to validate—don’t rush to calculate.

By securing this position, Uniswap is essentially taking a share of the infrastructure that institutions will use for the next wave of capital. What I can do isn’t to guess where it will swing.

Instead, I wait for it to overshoot—until it reaches the other side.

From this middle spot, it looks tempting and makes you itch to act, but that itch shouldn’t be a reason to place a bet.

Why BTC and #ETH  #BTC ?
They are more like the core assets of the entire Crypto market, while ETH is backed by a large number of decentralized applications and the blockchain ecosystem.

For beginners, understanding these two assets first is often more important than starting by searching for low-cap coins everywhere.

Many newcomers don’t lose money because they picked the wrong project—they lose because they love chasing pumps.

When a coin suddenly surges, you fear missing out, then rush in at the highest point of excitement. When the market pulls back, you realize you bought at the hottest spot.

That’s why DCA—dollar-cost averaging, investing periodically in batches—is essentially about reducing the risk of buying all at once at a high price.

Of course, this doesn’t mean BTC and ETH can’t fall. Crypto is still a high-volatility asset. Even BTC can go through very large cyclical drawdowns, and volatility in small-cap assets could even reach 70% or 90%.

So what’s truly important is not seeing others say BTC and ETH are worth paying attention to and rushing in immediately.

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation When Dusk Backpack announced that it would support real trading and even cover corporate actions like dividends for actual U.S. stocks, the industry went into an uproar. But behind the excitement, I saw a fatal vulnerability: right now, most “stock tokens” on the market can’t even accurately account for dividends at the underlying architectural level.

The root cause lies in how the token is constructed. The vast majority of on-chain assets use “single-dimensional” accounting—your account only shows one total position. However, determining dividend eligibility requires extremely precise time points: at the exact moment of the close on the ex-dividend date, who does the asset actually belong to? Remember, on-chain holdings are in constant motion. They may be transferring, earning interest while locked in a protocol, or becoming collateral for lending. Forcing all fluid states, lockup conditions, and ownership rights into a single number means the dividend distribution can only be “guessed” offline by the issuer.

This is also why I recently returned to re-examine $DUSK  and its Zedger mechanism. At the foundation, the model implements a highly forward-looking separation: it splits trading liquidity, voting and poll participation, and dividend proof/entitlement into three independent ledgers. That means even if your tokens are in the middle of a transfer, your eligibility to receive dividends remains solid. Even if the asset is in a pledged period, the power to participate in decisions is accounted for separately as well. With three tracks running in parallel, it perfectly avoids state conflicts.

Seen from the asset tokenization process, this is an absolute turning point. In the early days, everyone competed to hype the “putting assets on-chain” packaging. Then the focus shifted to the liquidity advantage of around-the-clock trading. But the true gate that eliminates low-quality projects comes in the third phase: “processing company-level actions.” Whether it can seamlessly handle dividends and stock splits determines whether it is truly an on-chain security—or merely a hollow price-tracking symbol.

Based on this, I’ve updated the evaluation framework for this sector: the ability to support trading is just the baseline; only the depth in handling traditional financial rights determines the ceiling of its value. Once the underlying logic is set, it can’t be undone or redone. So now, my assessment of DUSK’s goal is very specific: patiently wait for the Zedger architecture to be truly deployed and make the first real U.S. stock dividend distribution. The exact amount isn’t important. Its value is in proving to the market that the underlying infrastructure of this chain truly has the hard capability to carry the full operational cycle of traditional securities.#eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation 当 Dusk Backpack 宣布支持真实美股买卖，甚至包揽分红等公司行动时，圈内一片沸腾。但在热闹背后，我却看到了一个致命隐患：目前市面上大部分“股票代币”，其底层架构压根算不清派息这笔账。

核心症结藏在代币构造里。绝大多数链上资产采用“单维度”记账，账户里只显示一个持仓总量。然而，派息资格的认定需要极度精准的时间点——除权日收盘那秒钟，资产到底归谁？要知道，链上筹码是时刻流转的，它们或许正在转移，或许被锁在协议里生息，又或者变成了借贷抵押物。硬要把流动状态、锁仓情况和持股权益全压缩进一个数字，最后红利发放只能靠发行方在链下人工盲猜。

这也是我最近重新研究 $DUSK 及其 Zedger 机制的动因。该模型在底层做了一套极具前瞻性的拆分：将买卖流通、表决投票以及派息凭证分成了三个独立的账本。这意味着哪怕你的筹码正在转账，获取红利的资格依然稳固；即便资产处于质押期，参与决议的权力同样单独核算。三条线并行，完美避开了状态冲突。

站在资产代币化进程来看，这是个绝对的拐点。早期大家都在拼“资产上链”的包装噱头；随后焦点转移到全天候交易的流动性优势。但真正淘汰水货的关卡在于第三阶段：“消化公司级操作”。能否无缝衔接派息、拆股，决定了它究竟是真正的链上证券，还是仅仅是个虚有其表的价格追踪符号。

基于此，我更新了对该赛道的评判逻辑：撮合买卖的功能只是及格线，处理传统金融权益的深度才决定价值天花板。底层逻辑一旦定型就无法重来，所以现在审视DUSK的目标非常聚焦：耐心等待 Zedger 架构真正落地第一笔美股派息。具体金额不重要，它的价值在于向市场证明，这条链的底层基建，确实具备了承接传统证券完整运作周期的硬实力。#eth $ETH

From a macro perspective, by proactively increasing liquidity supply for long-dated U.S. Treasuries (10–20 years and 20–30 years), the Treasury is essentially easing potential pressure on long-term bond yields. When signals of “liquidity replenishment” are released on the Treasury side, global risk-asset discount-rate expectations may loosen slightly—crypto, as a high-beta asset, naturally reacts first.

Of note is that at the quarterly refinancing meeting on November 4, the Treasury will also disclose further arrangements regarding the subsequent repurchase scale. This may suggest that long-dated Treasury liquidity support is not a one-off measure, but rather a continuing variable throughout this refinancing cycle.

In the short term, improved expectations for macro liquidity provide the market with a mild tailwind. However, for the medium-to-long-term outlook, it still needs to be assessed comprehensively together with the Fed’s interest-rate path and employment and inflation data. Whether the positive news can translate into a sustained trend depends on the overall pace of repair in risk appetite.

Global government bond yields surge to multi-decade highs, while BTC $64,832 just lies there

On the same day, bond yields in the U.S., Japan, Germany, and France hit multi-decade highs; global liquidity tightens, and BTC is under pressure, moving sideways.

Last night wasn’t something going wrong in crypto—it was the entire bond market sending alarms. The intraday high for the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield touched 5.333%, the highest in nearly 20 years; Japan’s 10-year yield hit a new 30-year high; Germany’s 30-year returned to the 2011 level; and France’s is back to 2008 levels. This kind of situation across the four major economies happens only rarely in history. The Nasdaq 100 fell 1.3% that day, its biggest single-day drop in recent times. BTC has been trading around $64,832, up only about 1% in the past 24 hours, with no clear direction.

One-sentence translation: The cost of borrowing has become globally more expensive, all risk assets are being repriced, and BTC can’t dodge it.

Market impact
- Short term: A high-yield environment directly drains liquidity. Gold rose 8% this month, showing that risk-averse capital is running—but that money went into gold, not into BTC. Tonight’s Fed meeting minutes are a key variable: if the wording is hawkish, $64,832 won’t hold; if it’s dovish, there’s a chance for a rebound. ETH at $1,934 is weaker than BTC, and the risk of downside follow-through is higher.
- Medium term: Global yield curves keep steepening, which is a structural headwind for liquidity-sensitive assets like crypto. Institutional allocations will have to choose between high-yield bonds and crypto, and that situation won’t change—so the market is likely to stay choppy and somewhat bearish.

My take
Honestly, at this level I’m cautious. BTC managing to trade above $64,000 shows there is some support, but when the yields of the four major economies hit new highs at the same time—a macro combination like this—BTC has never won historically. Resistance is at $66,000; if $62,000 breaks, the pullback could accelerate quickly. ETH’s $1,900 is a key support—if it’s lost, more downside room opens up. Before tonight’s minutes are released, I don’t think there’s a clear directional setup. Standing by is more cost-effective than guessing direction. Risk point: Unexpectedly dovish minutes could trigger short-covering and a rebound—don’t treat a bearish view as a reason to go heavy.

当前价格靠近近24小时波动上沿，1小时 +0.76%、24小时 +1.95%。高位最重要的是确认突破后的接受度：价格能够留在上沿之上，说明市场认可更高区间；仅短暂刺穿后快速收回，则需要防范假突破。

第一条路径是向上：价格需要突破 1,943.21 并在其上方形成稳定收盘，随后回踩不破才算有效确认。第二条路径是向下：1,894 一旦失守且反抽无法收回，说明承接不足，应优先防守而不是急于补仓。

若价格继续停留在 1,943.21 与 1,894 之间，1,918.61 只作为短线主动权参考。区间中部没有明确优势，不为了参与感强行开仓，等市场把方向走出来。

对已有仓位的人，重点是按支撑是否失效来管理，而不是被每次波动带着走；对空仓的人，优先等待突破回踩或支撑确认。现货可以分批，合约则应缩短决策链条，先确定止损位置，再决定是否参与。

交易计划必须包含失效条件。判断正确可以分段兑现，判断错误也要允许自己退出，不能用加仓掩盖最初逻辑已经变化。行情会更新，观点也应跟随价格证据调整。

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  Today, since I’m free and nothing’s going on, I decided to move the $DUSK  I’ve been hoarding over to @Dusk_Foundation  on the mainnet to get some staking yield. Turns out it almost had me rage-quitting. I was holding ERC-20 assets on Ethereum, so I had to use the official bridge. After connecting both wallet ends and getting the authorization sorted, the fees weren’t even that bad—but the confirmation step was absolutely infuriating. I just sat there waiting for nearly ten minutes while the interface kept getting stuck on “status synchronization” with zero progress feedback. I thought the page had frozen, and I even hit F5 a bunch of times.

When the transfer finally succeeded, I opened my native wallet and—wow—there was nothing in it. I yelled at the official channel; only then did an admin reply that I needed to fill in the contract myself. I scoured the docs and finally found the address in some obscure corner. After studying it carefully, I realized this is actually a lock-and-mint setup: the Ethereum side locks the tokens, and then the other side mints them 1:1. But the unit precision differs wildly—ERC-20 uses 18 decimals by default, while native LUX uses 9. Because the underlying standards aren’t compatible, the frontend basically turned into a blindfold.

If a newcomer tries this, they’ll be completely lost on the spot.

I did the math myself. Add the toll for this trip and the operational wear-and-tear together—just to earn enough to break even on costs would take two to three months. And with the current market, if DUSK drops another leg, the interest you make won’t even cover the hole from principal shrinking. After thinking it through, I decided to hedge: I only transferred half the position over to test the experience, and the rest I left sitting on the exchange. After all, liquidity is king—if the chart looks off, you can dump and run faster than anything else.

Honestly, this mainnet has been running for a year and a half now, and Dusk Connect really is more user-friendly than back when it was mostly about key-importing. The technical chops are there too, and their two- or three-hundred-million-euro security-tokenization project with NPEX is genuinely hardcore in the RWA space. But right now it’s obvious they’re focused on integrations with institutions and big-picture narratives, while the infrastructure and user experience for retail users is terrible. I’ll keep my untouched positions where they are for now. I’ll only consider moving when the frontend interactions finally feel smooth. #eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  今天闲着没事，打算把囤的 $DUSK 提去 @Dusk_Foundation 主网弄点质押收益，谁知道差点给我整破防。手里拿的是以太坊 ERC-20 资产，必须走官方桥。连完两端钱包、搞定授权后，手续费倒是没扣多少，但等待确认的环节简直让人抓狂。干等了快十分钟，界面一直卡在状态同步，半点进度提示都没有，我还以为网页卡死了，吓得连按好几次 F5 刷新网页。

熬到转移成功，点开原生钱包一看，好家伙，里面空空如也！去官方频道吼了一嗓子，管理员才回复说要自己去填合约。翻遍了文档才在一个犄角旮旯找到地址。仔细研究才发现，这其实走的是 lock-and-mint 模式，两套底层在生硬对接：以太坊那边锁仓，这边再 1:1 铸造出来。而且单位精度天差地别，ERC-20 默认 18 位，原生 LUX 是 9 位。就因为底层标准不通用，前端直接成了瞎子。新人来搞绝对当场懵圈。

我自己拿笔算了一笔账：把这趟过路费和操作磨损加起来，光是把成本熬回来就得两三个月。现在这行情，万一 DUSK往下砸一波，赚的利息还不够补本金缩水的窟窿。思来想去，我决定防一手，只转了半仓过去体验，剩下的继续趴在交易所里。毕竟流动性才是王道，一旦盘面不对劲，直接砸盘跑路比什么都快。

讲真，这主网跑了一年半，现在的 Dusk Connect 确实比当年纯靠导密钥人性化不少。技术功底也在，跟 NPEX 搞的两三亿欧元证券代币化项目，在 RWA 圈子里算是实打实的硬核。但他们现在明显只顾着对接机构和做大叙事，散户的基建体验一塌糊涂。没动的仓位我先按兵不动，等哪天前端交互做丝滑了再考虑搬家。#eth $ETH

title: 🏦  التحليل المؤسسي للبيتكوين $BTC
subTitle:
التاريخ: 2026-08-19

---

## 1. الملخص التنفيذي
يظهر البيتكوين حالياً إشارة صعودية تكتيكية قوية على المدى القصير، وذلك بسبب وصول مؤشرات القوة النسبية (RSI) إلى مناطق تشبع بيعي شديدة على الإطارات الزمنية الصغيرة (RSI 16.61 على إطار 15 دقيقة)، بالإضافة إلى وجود جدار سيولة شرائية كبير (11.12 BTC). 

على الرغم من أن البيئة الكلية لا تزال تتسم بالحذر مع ارتفاع عوائد السندات والتوترات الجيوسياسية في الشرق الأوسط، إلا أن التوافق بين التحليلات الفنية قصيرة المدى وبنية العقود الآجلة (نسبة Long/Short تبلغ 1.4771) يشير إلى احتمالية عالية لحدوث ارتداد تصحيحي نحو مستوى 64,450. علماً بأن الاتجاهات الهيكلية طويلة المدى لا تزال تميل إلى الهبوط.

---

## 2. الاستخبارات الأساسية والماكرو
السياسة النقدية والاقتصاد الكلي:
- تضغط سوق السندات على الاقتصاد الحقيقي بينما تترقب الأسواق تحديثات جديدة من CNBC.

I originally planned to organize my thoughts before the weekend, but ended up finding screenshots of liquidation records from 4 a.m.

I still remember that sound now. My phone buzzed, and I immediately jumped up from the bed.

Red everywhere—my position was gone, and so was my sleep. Later I learned my lesson: I set stop losses on every single order.

Only after it hurt did I understand: a good trading system isn’t there to let you make how much money—it’s there to let you sleep at night.

Tonight I was flipping through a book and saw a line: “The market never punishes risk; it only punishes reckless ignorance.” —said by Livermore. I folded down the corner of this page.

Coincidentally, let’s look at today’s $ETH. 1,934—up 1.8% over the past 24 hours, with $301 million USDT in volume.

The volume isn’t big, and the volatility is slow and steady. But with this order book sitting there calmly, it feels like it’s reminding me: look, the days you don’t bet on direction are steady every night.

I didn’t understand this before. I didn’t set stop losses for my trades, and even mocked myself with “holding positions is a mindset.”

As a result, that slap at 4 a.m. left me unable to sleep well for half a month.

Citigroup wants to hand BTC custody to institutions: this time it’s not just hype, it’s real money custody services

Citigroup has launched its Custody+ platform plan to offer BTC custody, adding another piece of infrastructure for Wall Street’s old guard to step in.

This time, Citigroup isn’t just issuing bullish research reports—it’s doing business. The new Custody+ platform is targeting institutional clients and directly providing BTC custody. In plain terms, it’s a one-stop service for large funds like pension funds and family offices: securing private keys, record-keeping, and compliance. Custody doesn’t sound exciting, but it’s a prerequisite for institutions to enter—if the compliance department won’t approve it, even if institutions want to buy, they can’t get in. BNY Mellon and State Street have done it before; now a player of Citigroup’s scale is officially following through. Another legitimate spot for digital assets in the traditional financial system has been confirmed.

Market impact
Short term: BTC is currently at $64,490, and after the news the volatility is muted (up only +0.33% over 24h), suggesting the market has become somewhat immune to “traditional institutions entering” type of headlines—or that it doesn’t believe PPT and only believes fund flows. This kind of infrastructure-related positive catalyst doesn’t pull liquidity into the market as directly as an ETF does.

Medium term: this is the real focus. Custody → fund products → pension allocations: the chain is being built step by step. Citigroup’s compliance endorsement will give a batch of institutions that were on the sidelines an entry point. ETH $1,922 is also expected to benefit indirectly, because institutional infrastructure typically goes BTC first, then ETH.

One-sentence translation: the money hasn’t entered yet, but the door is being widened more and more.

My view
I’m moderately bullish, but the expectation needs to be set correctly: this isn’t a “pump tomorrow” headline; it’s a slow-moving variable over the next six months to two years. As long as BTC holds above $64,000, the medium-term structure hasn’t broken. The value of the institutional custody news lies in lowering the probability of a deep drawdown. The key risk is that if regulators keep flipping back and forth, these bank projects could be shut down at any time—back in 2022, they also didn’t do nothing.

I used to think the most worth talking about feature of TermMax was “fixed-rate lending,” until today when I opened its Earn page: the XAUt vault has TVL of about $23.31 million, RLUSD about $14.80 million, and another USDC vault about $5.72 million. What ranks at the top isn’t high-volatility altcoins, but tokenized gold, stablecoins, and dollar-denominated assets.
This setup made me rethink TermMax: it may be not only building a lending protocol, but also competing for an interest-rate pricing gateway after RWA goes on-chain.
There’s a clear difference between RWA and typical DeFi assets. Gold collateral, Treasury bills, or institutional credit often come with maturity dates, redemption rules, and relatively predictable cash flows. But many on-chain liquidity pools still use floating interest rates that change with utilization. The asset side has maturity terms, yet the cost of funds moves day by day—so a natural mismatch exists.#ETH 
TermMax’s fixed-maturity market can precisely plug this gap. Lenders buy discounted via FT and redeem at face value at maturity, locking in returns upfront; borrowers can also lock in their financing costs when establishing a position. For professional capital, “how much will the funds cost next month” may matter more than an extra few percentage points of APY today.
What’s truly worth watching is whether TermMax can organize capital with different maturity dates, collateral types, and risk appetites into an on-chain interest-rate curve with depth. If it can, what it offers won’t be just a yield entry point, but a financial rail along which RWA can be borrowed, lent, and priced.$NVDAB 
Of course, TVL doesn’t equal the model already being successful. Price sources, stablecoin credit, vault liquidity, maturity exit, and contract risk can all affect the outcome. Data can only show that capital is trying; it can’t replace risk judgment.
The question is: will RWA’s truly large-scale demand come first from “on-chain trading,” or from “predictable financing costs”? I lean toward the latter. What do you think?#termmax  @termmax

To be fair, the base-level blueprint crafted by @Dusk_Foundation  is extremely comprehensive, covering all dimensions such as payment flow circulation, node locking, and community governance. At first glance, it truly leaves no gaps.

As for the chip release rules, the official stance is quite rigid. The initial offering directly grants 500 million tokens, while the remaining 500 million is distributed gradually over a 36-year period, effectively sealing the supply ceiling at 1 billion tokens. At the same time, it introduces a Bitcoin-like four-year output halving mechanism. This kind of cliff-like reduction in emissions, in the long run, greatly alleviates market concerns about inflation.

However, hidden risks often lie in profit distribution. At present, nodes responsible for packaging blocks take as much as 80% of the system rewards. What does that mean? In large part, the current nodes’ excess returns are sustained by the system’s “printing.” But miners’ capital is always profit-seeking. Once the halving cycle arrives, the system “freebies” will be discounted significantly, and the motivation to maintain high-value locking will inevitably be greatly affected.

The ideal path everyone envisions goes like this: the on-chain ecosystem explodes—network interactions drive transaction fees through the roof—miners make a fortune—large capital rushes in to accumulate and lock up—available circulating tokens in the market become depleted. But for this script to play out smoothly, it must pass a life-or-death threshold: can the fee increment generated by real user contributions actually make up for the profit collapse caused by the system’s production reduction?

Put plainly, if advancing compliant privacy business for traditional finance is slow and there’s no real transaction volume to back it, those meager on-chain tolls can’t possibly support such a large node population. Once it’s not profitable, big players will withdraw their capital and unlock without hesitation. So, no matter how elegant the model design is, this is not an engine that can run automatically forever; in the end, it all comes down to whether external companies are truly willing to spend real money to consume Gas on-chain.#eth $ETH

在筹码的释放规则上，官方定得相当死。首发直接给足 5 亿枚，剩下的 5 亿枚额度则拉长到 36 年内逐步派发，彻底把整个盘子的天花板焊死在 10 亿枚。同时引入了类似比特币的四年产出减半机制，这种排放断崖式递减的做法，长线来看极大缓解了市场的通胀担忧。

不过，隐患往往出在利润分配上。现阶段，负责打包区块的节点拿走了高达 80% 的系统奖励。这意味着什么？当前节点的超额回报极大程度上是靠系统“印钞”来维持的。但矿工资本从来都是逐利的，一旦减半周期到来，系统白给的奖励大打折扣，维持高额锁仓的动力必然会大受影响。

大家设想的完美路径是：链上生态爆发——网络交互导致手续费飙升——矿工赚翻——吸引大资金抢筹锁仓——市面可流通筹码枯竭。但这套剧本想要顺利演下去，必须跨过一道生死门槛：真实用户贡献的手续费增量，究竟能不能补足系统减产带来的利润暴跌？

说穿了，要是面向传统金融的合规隐私业务推进缓慢，没有真实流水支撑，那点微薄的链上过路费根本养不活庞大的节点群体。一旦无利可图，大户就会毫不犹豫地撤资解锁。所以，无论模型设计得多精妙，这都不是能自动运转的永动机，最后拼的依然是到底有没有外部企业愿意真金白银地来链上消耗 Gas。#eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  After仔细琢磨了一下 $DUSK ’s tokenomics. As Dusk Network’s only fuel coin and core staking asset, combined with future on-chain voting rights, it indeed outlines a very coherent internal economic loop. From everyday transfers and payments, to node staking, to community governance, the application scenarios cover everything. Just looking at the design on the surface, this @Dusk_Foundation  setup is clearly well-structured and executed with precision.

When it comes to token supply, there is absolutely no ambiguity in the official rules. The initial circulating supply is 500 million tokens. After that, the inflation allowance capped for 36 years is also 500 million tokens; the overall hard cap for the entire network is capped at 1 billion tokens. On top of that, block rewards undergo a halving every four years, and this rapidly decaying release schedule can, in the long run, effectively suppress selling pressure.

But once I break down and thoroughly analyze the entire supply-and-demand model, I find that this closed loop hides a major risk: the profit-sharing structure for nodes is too heavily dependent on “newly distributed” supply. At present, block-producing nodes directly take 80% of the system rewards. Miners and capital are purely profit-driven—nobody is going to mine on love alone. Once the halving effect becomes prominent and the subsidy from inflation shrinks, the incentive to maintain staking will face serious problems.

The theoretical bullish logic is: as more on-chain assets accumulate, interactions become more frequent, Gas consumption skyrockets, nodes earn a windfall, which then attracts more people to lock up tokens, ultimately causing a sharp reduction in circulating tokens in the market. But for this logic to actually work, it hinges on a single bottleneck—can the growth rate of real network transaction fees truly outpace the speed at which block rewards shrink?

If the privacy business for compliant institutions still fails to gain traction for a long time, on-chain real activity will remain weak, and the meager transaction fees simply cannot fill the large shortfall left by the weakening of inflation. Once profits start to decline, the locked-up supply will loosen, or even trigger a chain of selloffs. In plain terms, this isn’t some kind of gravity-driven perpetual motion machine—it’s a fragile system with strict conditions attached. Whether it will ultimately work or not depends not on how loudly the mechanism is promoted, but only on whether there is truly scalable real-world business adoption on-chain. #eth $ETH

AI chips might be in short supply, not a real demand problem: investors start asking this awkward question

Market skepticism suggests the AI chip boom is an illusion caused by supply shortages. Once capacity expansion catches up, demand may not be as strong as people imagine.

According to Crypto Briefing, investors have raised a sharp challenge to the underlying logic behind AI infrastructure investment: did the surge in chip orders come from genuine demand, or from short-term shortages triggering panic hoarding?

The logic is simple: when everyone is afraid they won’t be able to buy chips, orders tend to self-amplify—real demand of 1 million chips turns into 1.8 million after stockpiling and rush buying. Once TSMC and others complete capacity expansions and delivery timelines shorten, these excess orders can evaporate instantly, leaving inventory build-up and surplus capacity.

In one sentence: the market isn’t short on chips—it’s short on “certainty,” and that’s exactly what capital fears the most.

Impact on the market
- Short term: sentiment is a bearish factor. Crypto markets have long been highly correlated with Nasdaq technology stocks, and the AI narrative has been one of the core stories supporting the valuation of risk assets over the past two years. As the narrative loosens, altcoins and AI-themed coins are likely to get hit first. BTC is currently trading sideways around $64,480.35 (up only +0.19% in 24h), suggesting the main funds were already in a wait-and-see mode and just need a reason to sell aggressively.
- Medium term: if AI capex slowdown is validated by data (capex guidance cut by cloud providers), liquidity assets like BTC will be repriced indirectly. ETH at $1,921.72 is down 0.97% in 24h; in a weak market structure, it’s more sensitive to macro narratives.

My take
I’m cautious. This challenge won’t instantly trigger a sell-off by itself, but it’s a sign of a narrative crack. Historically, every time a “this time is different” story gets questioned about the supply-side, it hasn’t been a good omen.

Scenario analysis: if BTC holds above around $64,000, it suggests the crypto market is still following its own halving-cycle logic, and AI noise is just noise. If it breaks, downside room could be significant. ETH at $1,900 is a key psychological level—if that breaks, it could accelerate the move. Risk point: if next week’s Nvidia earnings continue to blow expectations out of the water, this concern may be temporarily suppressed, and a rebound could follow.

My advice: don’t rush to bury the AI narrative, but it’s reasonable to adjust your position risk budget toward the conservative side.

逻辑很简单：当所有人都怕买不到芯片时，订单会自我放大——真实需求100万片，囤货抢购后变成180万片。等台积电们扩产到位、交付周期缩短，这些超额订单会瞬间蒸发，留下的是库存积压和产能过剩。

- 短期：情绪面利空。币圈跟纳斯达克科技股关联度一直很高，AI叙事是过去两年支撑风险资产估值的核心故事之一。叙事松动，山寨币和AI概念币先挨刀。BTC当前在$64,480.35附近横盘（24h仅+0.19%），说明主力资金本来就在观望，缺一个砸盘理由。

Investors are questioning whether the AI chip surge is fake prosperity distorted by shortages, not real demand—suggesting that sentiment in the tech sector should cool down.

Right now, AI chips are being snatched up, with longer lead times and higher prices. But one investor raised a hard-hitting question: is this “short supply” truly driven by demand, or is it simply that the supply chain can’t catch up in the short term?

The difference is crucial. If the shortage is demand-driven, manufacturers will aggressively expand capacity. Once that capacity is released, orders may not be as sticky, leading to inventory buildup, order cancellations, and price wars. The last chip cycle in 2022 collapsed in exactly this way: NVIDIA customers cut orders, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was halved—there’s even a “script” for it.

One-sentence translation: “Snatching up chips” now doesn’t necessarily mean we’ll need that many more chips in the future. The market may be mistaking a temporary shortage for permanent growth.

Impact on the market
- Short term: The AI narrative is an important support for the valuation of risk assets in this round (including BTC). If skepticism grows, tech stocks are likely to pull back, and the crypto market will almost certainly move down with them. BTC is currently consolidating around $64,480.35 with shrinking volume—it's waiting for direction.
- Medium term: If a confirmed inventory surplus emerges in 2026, the valuation of the entire AI chain will need to be repriced. Liquidity tightening will hit high-beta assets like crypto first. If BTC can’t hold up around $64,480, then the downside target is around the $77.5K range. ETH is weaker—$1,921.72 could easily retest the lows again.

Proving chip shortages as real takes time, and real execution needs to wait for inventory data in the earnings season—during that period, emotions will keep churning.

What’s going on
The Iranian parliament is discussing a bill that would authorize the military to take over the Strait of Hormuz. This strait is the lifeline of global oil—about 20% of the world’s oil shipments pass through it. If the bill passes, it effectively writes into law that Iran can “shut off” global oil routes at any time. That would directly heat up the situation in the Middle East. Oil prices would move first, then inflation expectations, and finally flow into the Fed’s rate path—this route has never been friendly to risk assets.

One-sentence translation: This isn’t a real blockade, but turning “possible blockade” into a legal option means the market must reprice geopolitical risk.

Market impact
- Short term: Safe-haven funds pull back first. High-volatility assets like BTC are hit first. Currently BTC is near $64,520; over the past 24h it’s only +0.32%, suggesting no panic yet—but once the news lands, a breakdown is only a matter of time. ETH $1,924 is weaker: despite a +1.18% bounce over 24h, if geopolitics turns negative, it will likely give back those gains.
- Medium term: If the strait is truly under military control, oil prices spike → inflation rebounds → rate cuts are delayed. This chain reaction would be a continuous draw of liquidity from crypto. Conversely, if the bill is merely used as a negotiation chip, the panic would be one-off.

My view
I’m bearish in the short term. At $64,520, BTC isn’t priced with panic, meaning the market hasn’t reacted yet—there’s room for the news to develop downward. Watch support around the $63,000 level: if it holds, it’s likely just emotion-driven volatility; if it breaks, expect a new round of deeper risk release. For ETH, I’m looking at $1,850. 📊 What Does "Timeframe" Mean in Trading? 🤔
If you are new to trading, you've definitely heard someone say:
"Check the 15m chart" or "Switch to the 1-Hour frame" 😅📈
Simply put, a Timeframe is the period of time that each single candle on the chart represents! ⏱️🕯️

For example 👇
🔹 1-Minute Frame (1m): Each candle tells you what happened to the price within 1 minute.
🔹 5-Minutes Frame (5m): Each candle represents 5 minutes.
🔹 15-Minutes Frame (15m): Each candle represents 15 minutes.
🔹 1-Hour Frame (1H): Each candle represents one full hour.
🔹 Daily Frame (1D): Each candle represents a whole day. 📅

Why is the Timeframe important? 👀
Smaller Timeframes: You see more details and faster movements ⚡, but there is also more noise and fake fluctuations.Higher Timeframes: The big picture of the market becomes clearer 📊, and you can see the true trend smoothly.

⭐ Example: On a 15-minute timeframe, candles close exactly at :00, :15, :30, and :45 of every hour.
⚠️ Remember: The timeframe alone doesn't tell you to buy or sell. It is just a tool to display price action within a specific period.

title: If You Can't Explain It, Don't Invest Yet.
subTitle:
A coin can be trending. A project can have thousands of followers. Influencers can be talking about it. The price can be rising quickly. But none of that answers the most important question: Do you understand what you're buying?
Before putting your money into a crypto asset, try to answer:
🔹 What problem does the project solve?
🔹 What is the token actually used for?
🔹 Who is building it?
🔹 How does the token supply work?
🔹 Where does its value come from?
🔹 What are the major risks?
🔹 What evidence supports your investment thesis? 
If you cannot explain the investment in simple language, that's not necessarily a reason to reject it. It's a reason to learn more before committing capital.
🔑 Key Takeaway: Understanding should come before conviction. Don't let a rising price create a conviction that research never created.
🧠 Practical Reflection; Before your next crypto investment, ask yourself: "If someone asked me why I own this asset, could I explain my reasons without mentioning its price?" If the answer is no, perhaps your next investment should be in knowledge first.
Thought for the Day. You don't need to understand every cryptocurrency. You only need to understand what you choose to put your money into.
Systems over emotion. Conviction over noise.

Strategy shareholders complain about the stock price, and the CEO lays it bare: buying us means buying BTC—don’t expect anything else

Strategy CEO responds to shareholders’ concerns over the share price: the company’s positioning is a BTC leveraged exposure, not a short-term trading tool.

Phong Le steps in to reassure shareholders. Put simply, it’s one stance: Strategy’s core value is to provide shareholders with BTC exposure. Short-term share price fluctuations are not the management team’s top priority. Since the company holds a large amount of BTC, the linkage between the share price and the coin price matters far more than the linkage between the share price and the company’s own operating performance. If shareholders are looking for a “steady growth stock,” then they’re definitely in the wrong place. This response makes no promise of buybacks or share-price boosting actions—it effectively puts “long-term holding, take it or leave it” right on the face of it.

One-sentence translation: The CEO didn’t save the stock price—he only reiterated the game rules: what you’re buying isn’t the company, it’s a basket of BTC.

Market impact
- Short term: neutral to slightly positive. Management isn’t panicking, indicating there’s no pressure from forced BTC selling. That’s good news for BTC’s $64,368.18 holder structure. But if MSTR shareholder sentiment continues to build, the premium could narrow, weighing on some indirect buy orders coming through the stock market.
- Medium term: Strategy is already one of the largest publicly listed buyers in the BTC spot market. As long as its “hold-no-matter-what” strategy is maintained, circulating supply keeps tightening. How long shareholders can tolerate a calm, flat share price is the biggest variable in this model.

My take
View: neutral to bullish. BTC’s current price is $64,368.18, and over the past 24h it has moved only 0.34%, suggesting the market is digesting this kind of news with steady sentiment. Management has clearly stated they won’t sell coins. One of the biggest potential sources of selling pressure is ruled out, which is more tangible than any headline reassurance. ETH $1,918.27 tracks the broader market, up 1.15% in 24h. The risk is that if the stock price underperforms BTC for the long run, shareholders may “vote with their feet” by rotating into directly holding BTC, causing Strategy’s buyback/accumulation engine to slow and indirect demand to weaken. This structural risk is worth watching, but it likely won’t smash the market in the short term.
